resource.name: PM Ladder Self-Assessment
resource.description: Thirty questions across five PM career dimensions. Returns effective level, gap report, three behaviors for the quarter, and an optional manager-calibration delta.

tools.name: pm_ladder_score
tools.description: Deterministic. Returns per-dimension levels, the overall effective level, and the widest-gap target dimension for the next level.

answers.description: Thirty answers in question-ID order. Each answer is a level (1-5).

tools.name: pm_ladder_narrate
tools.description: LLM-narrated gap report and three behaviors to practice this quarter, anchored in corpus chunks.

tools.name: pm_ladder_calibrate
tools.description: LLM-narrated calibration delta. Reads the user's self-scoring alongside their manager's last review and returns the dimensions of widest disagreement with discussion questions for the next 1:1.

manager_review_text.description: The text of the user's last performance review from their manager.

tools.name: pm_ladder_drift
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Stores scoring across runs and reports drift versus prior runs. The tool stores state locally and is not read-only — hosts will surface a confirmation prompt on first invocation.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.phase_note: Web/URL-trick versions don't expose this tool. State requires the MCP App; host's confirmation UI handles the consent surface.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #3 PM Ladder Self-Assessment. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. Validated against MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026 release + current draft) on 2026-05-18.

dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.summary: Narration tools in this app return a narration_brief, not the structured prose directly. The outputSchema(s) defined above describe the target rendering structure the host chat model is asked to produce. At runtime each narration tool returns { type: 'narration_brief', audience: 'user', directive, voice_rules, structure: { sections, per_section_template, length_cap }, inputs: <tool-specific>, corpus: { anchor_slug: chunk_text } }. The host chat model then renders the user-facing prose from the brief.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.worked_example: bundle/src/tools/pm-pitfalls/narrate.ts and bundle/src/shared/schemas.ts (PitfallNarrateOutput). Sonnet clones this pattern for every narration tool listed below.
dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.supersedes: Earlier 'host sampling + api_key fallback' design. Sampling/createMessage was not exposed by Claude Desktop or Claude Code CLI to user-installed extensions in 2026-05; Path 4 makes the host chat model the renderer, which is the MCP-recommended idiom.

dev.workingfromlenny.open_questions: Confirm the 8000-char manager_review_text upper bound covers the typical written review (most are 1500-4000 chars).
Decide how pm_ladder_drift signals to the host that it is stateful — readOnlyHint: false on the tool annotation is the only normative hook.
dev.workingfromlenny.proposed_answers: 8000 chars is safe. Typical written reviews run 1,500-4,000 chars; the 8000 cap is roughly double the high end, covering verbose orgs. It is not so large that it creates prompt-bloat risk when the review text feeds into the narration call. Keep 8000.

Use the tool-level annotations.readOnlyHint: false hint (now set above). The MCP Apps spec leaves consent UX to host discretion — there is no manifest-level data-retention or requires-consent flag. The host's confirmation UI handles per-call or install-time consent however that host chooses. Document persisted data in the tool description so the host's confirmation can convey it (dimension_levels + effective_level + timestamp per run; no full answer text).

notes: ui:// scheme is valid; no rigid format is enforced — server-defined slugs after the scheme are acceptable.

No requires-consent / data-retention / fs-write capability exists in either ext-apps appCapabilities or .mcpb manifest. Consent is host-discretion; readOnlyHint: false on stateful tools is the only normative hook.
Underscore-prefixed fields at non-_meta paths have undefined host behavior; project metadata lives under _meta with reverse-DNS keys.
